text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Shockwaves in the right-wing Disy party after disclosures by its president that he is being 'undermined' by other party members.
- Cyprus's maritime industry causes concern to the European Union.
- Disy and Diko will probably announce their decision to support joint candidates during municipal elections next week.
- Civil servants union Pasydy organise a united front against government-planned privatisations.
- President Glafcos Clerides accepts United Nations plan for indirect military talks with the other side.
- House of Representatives approves a 2.5 percent pay rise to civil servants from January.
- Parliamentarians debate tougher penalties on illegal workers.
- Crisis looms in Disy party - President Clerides is expected to announce a cabinet reshuffle in November.
- Implementation of civil defence plans in the event of a war is a grey area for the government.
- Meat unfit for human consumption is on the market, say butchers.
- President Clerides intends running for a second presidential term, says the government spokesman.
